source: Spec 124 R-DA (McDonald's Airtight V3): every entry is the measured PRE -> POST diff of docs/reports/golden/classify_coa_trades/{pre,post}/{coa,standalone}.json (Night A-swap 2026-10-22, lane COA-ASWAP, back-to-back under the dblock: PRE retaken on the LEGACY shell, the R-EQ shell swap applied, POST taken on the converted shell), explained from the descriptor deviation, register rule, runner code or the captures' own measured values it names. table_state[].content_hash is the one data key that moves: the plain POST captures were retaken after the forced bracket (a compute fix, empty-cursor zero counters, forced the retake; R-DQ orders plain before bracket) and so read the classified_at stamps the bracket rewrote on 50 CoAs (880 lead_trades / lead_products rows). Row counts are equal.

diffs.why: PIPELINE_META is derived from the descriptor outputs.writes (Spec 122 §5.1, R-BJ): the coa_applications write target lists [id, trade_classified_at] (key first); the legacy hand-written meta listed [trade_classified_at, id]. Same column set.

R-EQ shell swap: the legacy shell hand-printed JSON-log lines ("Loaded 35 trade configs / 805 logic variables from control panel", the classification progress and summary lines) and a hyphenated completion line; the runner prints its own lines (the target line "database=postgres user=postgres migrations=<n>", the ledger-gate line where the step gates, the PIPELINE_SUMMARY and PIPELINE_META lines and one "[classify_coa_trades] completed in <DUR>" line). Log lines only: no table, counter or verdict value is read from them, and the PIPELINE_SUMMARY content is diffed separately in the summary.* keys.
The runner titles the audit table with the descriptor identity.display_name "Classify CoA Trades"; the legacy literal was "CoA Trade Classification". The consumer reads rows, not the name.

audit_table.phase follows sharing.varies_by_chain.phase, the step's 1-based coa-chain index 7, generated by scripts/generate-sharing-phase.js (LCTP-D8 / the O1 fleet standard); the legacy literal was 42.
The library stamps every declared check row with observed before_write / after_write (FLEET-2 lib #52); the legacy hand-built rows had no such field.

The library stamps every declared check row with source "check" and every compute context row with source "context" (verdict.js checkRow / contextRow); the legacy hand-built rows carried no source field.

The converted table holds the declared checks only (coa_eligible, unmapped_scope_pct, avg_active_trades_per_lead, slug_resolution_miss_count, product_slug_miss_count, realtor_unavailable and the two vocab-coverage rows) so rows shift against the legacy order; coa_eligible renders WARN on the settled POST (descriptor check coa_eligible, limit value_min 1, severity WARN: "an empty cursor WARNs", legacy :460-465, pinned L16) where the legacy PRE read PASS on 2,334 processed. Verdict WARN, not a failure.

The library renders the declared limit in force (e.g. "viol == 0", "pct <= 10") on each declared check row; the legacy rows carried the limit as prose or not at all. The bound is the step-owned variable in summary.records_meta.config.

deviations[0] (operator y 2026-10-18): the legacy audit values were display strings ("20.0%", "N/A") and moved with the row order; the converted rows carry the measured number or the check detail. Values differ because of the ordering effect: Measured ordering effect, not a behaviour change: the legacy PRE coa capture was the first trades run after scope's own PRE did the pending work, so the legacy shell classified the 2,334 pending CoAs (599 new and 35,954 updated lead_trades / lead_products rows); the converted POST then ran on the settled state, streamed nothing (the R-EX rerun proof PASS, zero writes on lead_trades, lead_products and coa_applications) and read 0. The nonzero evidence is the separate coa-forced.json bracket.

Row order and membership follow the declared check set (Spec 132 §core.6: the verdict comes only from check rows; §core.11: dynamic tallies ride a check row detail; deviations[0], deviations[2]): the legacy table listed 26 rows (descriptive tallies such as coa_with_trades, coa_zero_trades, avg_trades_per_lead, the evidence / inference tallies, records_new / records_updated and the product tallies); the converted table lists the 10 declared rows, with the per-trade tallies carried as the detail of avg_active_trades_per_lead (R-EP). A descriptive tally the descriptor does not declare as a check is no longer rendered as a row.

A declared check with a warn tier (warn_limit, 124a R-AD) renders its warn limit as warn_threshold; the legacy rows had no such field. Here the two vocab-coverage checks (trade_vocab_coverage, product_vocab_coverage: pct >= 90, warn pct >= 70; the legacy cov_ rows had no rendered bound).
Row count: the legacy table has 26 rows, the converted table 10 (deviations[0], deviations[2]; Spec 132 §core.6); the trailing legacy rows have no converted counterpart at the same index.

Coa capture: the legacy PRE read PASS; the converted POST reads WARN (the standalone PRE already read WARN on its empty cursor) solely from coa_eligible (value_min 1, WARN) on an empty cursor (legacy WARN branch, pinned L16). No check is FAIL. The forced bracket capture reads WARN as well (880 rows rewritten, avg_active_trades_per_lead detail).

Nothing is lost: the chain capture shows no row in either side.
